newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius conglomerate Rogers opens bonds sale.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius conglomerate Rogers opens bonds sale.

text.p: Mauritius largest conglomerate Rogers opened on Tuesday a sale issue of 200 million rupees ($9.89 million) of secured bonds to finance the group's major investments and capital projects.
Company officials said that the bonds, with a coupon rate of 10.5 percent per annum, were being sold at their nominal value of 1,000 rupees each, in a sale issue that closes on March 20.
The 200 million rupees raised will be used to finance Rogers' ventures in areas such as the freeport, leasing, paint production, warehousing and bottling facilities.
"Most of the projects have already started and are progressing according to the group investment programme," a Rogers' official said.
Rogers bonds have a maturity date of 19 March 2002 but early redemption of the securities can occur at the discretion of the company after 19 March 2000, the official added.

Officials said that out of the 200 million rupees on issue, 50 million rupees were earmarked for private placement with local commercial banks and the remaining 150 million rupees were available for public sale.
The Rogers bonds were expected to be quoted on the Stock Exchange of Mauritius in April.

In the year to 30 September 1996, Rogers profit before tax slipped to 423.7 million rupees from 428.6 million rupees one year earlier. Turnover was posted at 8.67 billion rupees in 1995/96 up from 7.97 billion rupees in 1994/95.
Rogers is forecasting a profit before tax of 490 million rupees for the financial year ending 30 September 1997.
